_meta.what: The few destinations worth shipping: present on essentially every developer machine, and carrying something a tool schema does not show — which flag holds the body, that a tracked file is one somebody will read, that a commit message has no addressee so the judgement checks have nothing to ask. Everything else is found by /prose-guard:setup, which can see the tool list this file cannot.
_meta.extend: Put a file with this shape at <config dir>/destinations.json. Your entries are tried BEFORE these, so you can override one as well as add one. /prose-guard:setup will offer to write it for you, from what it finds on your machine.
_meta.match: tool: matched as a substring of the tool name, so MCP prefixes need not be spelled out. bash: a regex over the command. file: a regex over file_path.
_meta.identifiers: Which tool-call fields carry the channel, repo, owner or path. audiences.json matches on these, so a destination with no identifiers can never resolve an audience.
_meta.text: text_fields: input fields that may hold the prose. text_arg: for Bash, flags whose value is the prose; a flag ending in -file is read from disk.

destinations.name: commit message
destinations.note: everyone who reads this repository's history, including you in a year. It is permanent and it is not edited later.
destinations.caveat: Only the forms that put the text on the command line can be seen. `git commit` with no -m opens an editor, and that text never reaches the tool call. And it is checked at `low` whatever level you set: the terms check only, no model call. A commit message has no addressee and no ask, so most of what the higher levels ask does not apply to it.

destinations.name: prose file someone will read
destinations.note: whoever reads this file later, without you present

when._edit: an edit to an existing document: judge the change, not the whole document

destinations.caveat: require_tracked means the file must sit in a git working tree and not be ignored. That is the difference between a document colleagues will read and a scratch file: one gets committed.

public_owners_help: Repository owners whose content outsiders can read. Declared rather than guessed, because telling someone a private repository is public makes them strip links their colleagues could have opened.
